limitations: Source-derived candidate; no local efficacy validation.
Original typed source inventory is not normalized; retain source identities and limits in the procedure/readsets.

applicability.scope: Audit Linux cgroup v2 CPU quota/shares, effective placement, memory pressure/protection and conditional block-device IO controls for serving or training workloads.
applicability.prerequisites: Identify workload cgroup membership, kernel/controller support, ancestor limits and the authorized file owner; prepare previous values and stop conditions before a separately authorized trial.
applicability.input_contract: Target PID and hierarchy/namespace view, requested/effective cpusets, time-aligned CPU/memory/IO counters and application/sibling observations; IO proposals require resolved block-backed traffic.
applicability.produced_artifact: An evidence-qualified control review/proposal with capacity tradeoff, configuration provenance, rollback manifest and matched-window application/sibling checks.
applicability.failure_modes: Ancestor constraints can invalidate requested placement; pressure movement alone is not application causality, and unsupported IO accounting or shared-inode attribution can misassign traffic.

recommendations: Separate own-quota throttling, ancestor limits and sibling contention before choosing a cpu.max or cpu.weight review.
Compare requested with effective CPU/node sets and budget cpuset.mems migration before proposing placement; align memory PSI with local versus descendant event deltas.
Treat increased headroom as a shared-capacity spend and verify application outcomes and sibling impact, not just counter improvements.
Resolve actual block-backed traffic and supported IO controls before proposing caps; preserve inaccessible-ancestor uncertainty and do not infer container write authority.
